# Topology and Ambiguity Handling
## Overview
Topology and Ambiguity Handling resolves topological inconsistencies in standard lookup-table-based isosurface extraction when the isosurface passes through saddle points within a voxel [S1]. Standard lookup tables assign a fixed triangulation to ambiguous cases (e.g., 46, 47, 98, 99, 210, 213, 214, 215), which can cause cracks or holes if adjacent voxels resolve the ambiguity differently [S1]. Unlike [Lookup Table and Configuration](4978-lookup-table-and-configuration.md) which focuses on table generation, or [Marching Cubes Isosurface Tie-Breaking](10380-marching-cubes-isosurface-tie-breaking.md) which handles exact isovalue hits, this family enforces global manifold consistency through local patch or Hermite data constraints.
## Shared principles
The family addresses the ambiguous case problem where the 8-bit sign pattern of a voxel's vertices does not uniquely determine the isosurface topology [S1]. In these configurations, the isosurface passes through the cube center, creating a saddle point [S1]. All methods in this family enforce local consistency across voxel boundaries to ensure the output mesh is a topological manifold, preventing cracks or non-manifold vertices that arise when adjacent voxels resolve the ambiguity inconsistently [G].
## Subtopics

### [Hermite Dual Marching Cubes](2197-hermite-dual-marching-cubes.md)
A surface extraction method that guarantees a topological manifold mesh by leveraging Hermite data (intersection points and normals) and minimizing a Quadratic Error Function (QEF). Unlike standard Dual Contouring, which may produce non-manifold artifacts in ambiguous configurations, this method uses the dual structure of Nielson’s Dual Marching Cubes to enforce connectivity. Choose this method when sharp feature preservation is required alongside strict manifold guarantees.

### [Marching Cubes with Disjoint Patch Decomposition](5004-marching-cubes-with-disjoint-patch-decomposition.md)
A topology resolution method that decomposes the isosurface intersection within a voxel into disjoint connected components (patches) using a tetrahedral decomposition graph. Unlike standard lookup tables that may produce non-manifold joints in saddle-point configurations, this method uses graph-based edge coloring to group cut edges into distinct patches. Choose this method when consistent manifold generation is needed for complex saddle-point scenarios without relying on Hermite data.
